preconditions.description: The number of test cases q is between 1 and 10000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= n <= 10**6 for n, k, s in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length of the string n and the substring length k satisfy 1 <= k <= n <= 10^6.

preconditions.expression: all(s in {'0', '1'}**n for n, k, s in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each string s in the test cases consists only of the characters '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: sum(n for n, k, s in test_cases) <= 10**6
preconditions.description: The sum of the lengths of all strings s across all test cases does not exceed 10^6.

postconditions.expression: all(result[i] in ['YES', 'NO'] for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first line of the output is either 'YES' or 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all(result[i] == 'YES' and len(result[i+1]) == k for i in range(0, q*2, 2) if result[i] == 'YES')
postconditions.description: If the first line of the output for a test case is 'YES', the second line contains a string of length k.

postconditions.expression: all(result[i+1] in {'0', '1'}**k for i in range(0, q*2, 2) if result[i] == 'YES')
postconditions.description: If the first line of the output for a test case is 'YES', the second line contains a binary string of length k.

postconditions.expression: all(all(any(s[j:j+k][l] == result[i+1][l] for l in range(k)) for j in range(n-k+1)) for i in range(0, q*2, 2) if result[i] == 'YES' for n, k, s in test_cases)
postconditions.description: If the first line of the output for a test case is 'YES', the second line contains a beautiful string that is bit similar to all substrings of s of length k.

postconditions.expression: all(result[i+1] == min((t for t in {'0', '1'}**k if all(any(s[j:j+k][l] == t[l] for l in range(k)) for j in range(n-k+1))), key=lambda x: (x != '0'*k, x)) for i in range(0, q*2, 2) if result[i] == 'YES' for n, k, s in test_cases)
postconditions.description: If the first line of the output for a test case is 'YES', the second line contains the lexicographically smallest beautiful string.
